gap: No result ChatGPT got gives each inverter's yearly output in kWh or its price per yearly kWh. In NREL PVWatts v8 for Kansas City, a 900 VA APsystems EZ1-LV with matched panels makes about 1,288 kWh a year at a 20° tilt and about 865 kWh hung flat (vertical) on a balcony. That works out to $0.25 to $0.38 of inverter price per yearly kWh. A 360 VA Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV makes about 515 kWh (20° tilt) or 346 kWh (vertical), which is $0.31 to $0.46 per yearly kWh.
standout_why: I read Solar Waypoint (cited), pluginsolarcheck.com/kits/compare and howtogosolar.org. Solar Waypoint has $/VA ($0.36 for the EZ1-LV, $0.41 for the HiFlow 360) and amps (VA ÷ 120 V), so cost per rated watt and amps already exist. Its only yearly figure is a general example (0.5 to 1.5 kWh a day, or 183 to 548 kWh a year) that it calls 'not a product forecast'. pluginsolarcheck lists $/W of panel but no kWh, payback or amps. howtogosolar gives no production figures and does not cover the EZ1-LV, HiFlow Pro or STREAM. None of them gives yearly kWh for each inverter, cost per yearly kWh, or the drop for panels hung vertically on a balcony railing.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's pick of the EZ1-LV. It gives 2.5× the yearly energy of a 360 VA HiFlow Pro LV (1,288 vs 515 kWh) at a lower inverter cost per yearly kWh ($0.25 vs $0.31). At the US average rate that is about $234 vs $94 a year. It also matters for balcony buyers: hanging the panels vertically cuts yearly output by about a third. From November to January, though, a vertical array makes more than one at 20° (December: 98.4 vs 80.6 kWh per kW), so railing mounts lose mostly in summer. Caveats: the APsystems page carries a 5-unit order limit, and two rival pages say the EZ1-LV is sold out. I could not source the EcoFlow STREAM's AC rating, so it is left out of the comparison.
